10. Health and safety management system:
a.
Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the
entity? (Yes/No). If yes, the coverage such system?

Yes, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Standard is being adopted at the Bank. During FY2025, three
new locations were added, taking the total to 21 premises like large offices, call centres, data centres, learning centre
and staff quarters.
b.
What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and
non-routine basis by the entity?

The Bank has a process for identifying work related hazards, including collecting and reviewing all available
information about potential and actual problems and periodic inspection of the workplace. A systematic approach
has been adopted which involves division of the workplace into major areas like workstation, utility, storage,
processing, customer service, and others, and with appropriate measures identified for the respective locations. The
Bank has established a robust process for dealing with electrical and fire hazards including regular testing, ensuring
use of protective equipment and training for emergency preparedness. Also, effective work permit system is in place
to improve operational efficiency, enhance safety & security exposure and reduce risk of accidents within the Bank’s
premises.

Assessment of significant risk involves:

1.
Identifying potential hazards and risks associated with specific activities, processes or environments through
Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA);

2.
Evaluating likelihood and potential consequences of these risks;

3.
Prioritizing risks based on their significance and potential impact on safety, health, and the environment;

4.
Developing strategies to control, reduce, or eliminate significant risks through engineering controls, administrative
controls, and/or personal protective equipment (PPE);

5.
Periodically reviewing and reassessing risks to ensure ongoing effectiveness of risk management measures.

At the Bank’s large offices, key activities include maintaining inventory of materials and material safety data sheets
(MSDS), periodic testing of premises for air, noise and illumination quality, an online system for recording safety
related complaints from employees, and log of maintenance of the premises. Further, there is ongoing evaluation of

Describe the internal mechanisms in place to redress grievances related to human rights issues.

disciplinary process is carried out. Disciplinary procedure would start after detailed fact finding exercise/internal
investigation including one-to-one discussion with the concerned employee, where-ever possible-by the respective
business group and a detailed report to that effect is submitted to the human resources management group for
taking the necessary action. Such investigation is carried out independent of the respective business group.

Whistle Blower Policy: An employee may send communication through e-mail to chairman.auditcommittee@
icicibank.com or head.whistleblower@icicibank.com. The employee may also send a communication directly in
writing through a letter to Chairman, Audit Committee or to General Counsel of ICICI Bank Limited. Additional modes
of communication or access may be made available to employees in appropriate or exceptional situations.

The Bank is committed to protection of the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases. In cases covered
under the Policy against Sexual Harassment at workplace, the complainant is provided protection as under:

•
Proceed on paid leave till closure of investigation (on request by the complainant).

•
Temporary posting to another branch/office till closure of investigation (on request by the complainant).

•
100% confidentiality on the case details, complainant and respondent.

In whistle blowing cases, the identity of the whistle blower is not revealed. The Bank also does not tolerate any
attempt on the part of anyone to retaliate, to cause disadvantage or to discriminate against any person who has
reported to the Bank serious and genuine concerns regarding an apparent wrong-doing. Protection under the policy
is available to the employee who raises the concern under this policy till such time that the complainant’s employment

The Bank has a defined Business Continuity Management (BCM) (including disaster management) plan to ensure
continuity of critical services to customers and availability of critical systems during significant disruptions under
defined disaster scenarios. In the event of a disaster, the Bank endeavours to resume business and operations to an
acceptable level as per the defined Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) detailed in the plan. The RTO provides guidance
for prioritizing activities, whenever necessary. There can be external factors beyond the Bank’s control, which could
affect the actual RTO. The BCM plans are reviewed and maintained to incorporate changes in the organization or

1.
Describe the mechanisms in place to receive and respond to consumer complaints and feedback.

The Bank complies with the 'Customer Rights Policy' which enshrines the basic rights of customers including Right to
Grievance Redress and Compensation. The Bank has made it easy and seamless for customers to raise complaints
through multiple channels including the business centres, voice, and digital channels. The Bank has a Board
approved Customer Grievance Redressal Policy which outlines the well-defined framework to address customer
complaints ensuring fair, transparent, and timely resolution with clear turnaround times. All complaints are recorded
in a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system and tracked for end-to-end resolution. An escalation matrix
built in the CRM system ensures that customer requirements are appropriately addressed within stipulated timelines.
Detailed Root Cause Analysis (RCAs) of the issues highlighted in customer feedback, complaints, etc. are conducted
and insights from the same are implemented to improve the products and processes and enhance services of the
Bank. As recommended by the Reserve Bank of India, senior retired bankers are appointed as Internal Ombudsmen
of the Bank. The Customer Service Committee of the Board, the Standing Committee on Customer Service and the
business centre level Customer Service Committees monitor customer service at different levels.

The Bank aims to treat its customers fairly and provide transparency across its offerings. Continuous customer
education efforts are made to enable customers to make informed choices regarding banking products and
services. The Bank also seeks to ensure that the products offered are based on an assessment of the customer’s
financial needs.

The Bank regularly conducts customer awareness campaigns through social media, notifications on mobile apps,
e-mails and SMS (in regional language also) regarding safe banking, cybersecurity as well as modus operandi of
frauds prevalent in society. The Bank displays the awareness messages during new payee addition, high value fund

The Bank also displays relevant messages at its offices and business centres for customer awareness. The Bank has
been conducting extensive public awareness campaigns on fraud prevention on television and social media since
FY2022. The #BeatTheCheat campaign spreads awareness on the modus operandi and pretext used by fraudsters
to defraud the customers. The videos are made in 11 regional languages, and has been well-received. Topics
covered various forms of fraud including fake lottery emails, fake QR codes, fake apps and parcel/digital arrest scam,
providing scenarios and fraud prevention tips. Further, recognizing financial literacy as a need for customers’, the
Bank introduced “The Orange Book”, a monthly e-magazine in English and Hindi languages that covers an array of
financial topics from investment planning, safe banking to tax savings, financial preparedness and much more.

The Bank has a Customer Communication & Response Committee (CCRC) to manage customer communication and
responsiveness of the Bank in case of system incidents. CCRC has representation from relevant internal stakeholder
groups including customer service, business, channels, technology, corporate brand and communications, risk, credit
monitoring, etc. Further, in the event of disruption or a disaster, the Bank has put in place mechanisms for customers
to contact the Bank, details of which are also available on the Bank’s website.

recommend, satisfaction levels with the product/transaction experience and voice of customer (VOC) are measured.
Approximately, 3.8 million customers were covered for their feedback. This feedback is analysed and the insights
